messages:
samir: Quick check — we peered svc-vpc (vpc-0a1b2c) with infra-vpc. Service needs to send telemetry to metrics.example.com (443). Do we allow outbound 0.0.0.0/0 via NAT from the service subnet, or should we proxy through infra egress? Also any logging redaction concerns when hitting the vendor?

maria_r: Do we have vendor IP ranges? They only provide FQDNs. If they don't publish static IPs we should avoid direct NAT egress. Recommend proxy/PrivateLink. If NAT, must have allowlist + rotation + audit.

jen-ops: who owns the infra-vpc route table? I can check.

jen-ops: quick check — service subnet route table shows default to nat-rtb (nat-0aa1b2) and peering to pcx-12ab. Looks like egress exits infra-vpc IGW currently.

alex.h: route excerpt I pulled:
```
# route table for subnet-abc
Destination: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0aa1b2
Destination: 10.10.0.0/16 -> pcx-12ab
```
So vendor traffic leaves via NAT in infra-vpc. That means metrics vendor will see our public egress IPs — if they require an allowlist we need stable IPs or a proxy.

sec-bot: [AUTOMATED] DNS check: metrics.example.com resolves to a CNAME -> cloudfront.net; no stable IPs detected. Risk: dynamic IPs. Recommendation: use VPC endpoint / PrivateLink or an internal proxy that presents stable egress IPs.

samir: OK. Can infra spin up an internal proxy in infra-vpc and we point the service at it? Also we need to make sure outgoing request/response logs redact PII (user ids/emails). Who owns logging filters in svc?

maria_r: Logging note: current svc emits full request bodies at debug in prod — please stop. Use our logging lib mask_fields option. Example config: mask_fields=["email","user_id","authorization"]. I'll open a PR to enforce in the repo CI.

lina: Infra security policy: any new public egress to a third-party requires a JIRA ticket + TTL and owner. Temporary allowlists are allowed but need rotation plan.

jen-ops: I'll stand up a small squid proxy behind an internal ALB in infra-vpc and lock SG to only the service subnet. We can route via env proxy (HTTP_PROXY). ETA end of day to prototype.

samir: Nice. For approvals — can infra-approvals-bot pre-check low-risk egress for metrics ports? Tagging @infra to confirm.

infra-approvals-bot: Approval workflow: please create JIRA INFRA-REQ with scope, owner(s), TTL, and justification. Use template: "Allow outbound 443 to metrics.example.com via internal ALB proxy, TTL 7 days, owners: jen-ops, samir". Attach test plan and IP rotation schedule.

alex.h: Also add env var to redact logs: LOG_REDACT_PATTERNS="(email|user_id|ssn)" and mark PR for sec review.

samir: I'll file the JIRA and a PR for the logging changes and link both here. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jen-ops: quick follow-up: should we also block direct DNS resolution to the vendor from the service subnet and force resolution in infra-vpc (proxy)? avoids split-brain DNS.

maria_r: Yes, force resolution through proxy or use conditional forwarding. We'll add that to the ticket.

samir: Filed INFRA-1789 and PR: github.com/redwood/svc/pull/234 — tagging for review, will update when proxy ready.
